proof_attempt_summary: The run reframed the two-class signed minimax theorem and Pareto frontier with a distinct minimal three-class extension, then performed a bounded primary-source priority revision that increased verified sources from four to five. Soundness and structure remained clean, but the final Gabler–Stenger 2000 theorem text or an authoritative corresponding precursor could not be obtained, so field novelty could not be cleared; the constructive mathematics remains suitable for a subfield re-raise once that comparison is available.
tldr: For exact-budget randomization with two prescribed propensity values, ask for the smallest worst variance over a fixed signed-score ellipsoid at every requested level of same-sign variance protection. The proposed answer is an exact integer-feasible, closed Pareto frontier with an explicit count-mixture sampler and a sharp criterion for when nonpositive covariance costs signed robustness. A mirrored four-unit, three-propensity family probes the first extension beyond two classes.
gap: General spectral minimax bounds and nonpositive-covariance safeguards do not determine which covariance matrices are realizable under a fixed budget and fixed unequal marginals, or the precise cost of that safeguard for signed scores.
fill: Establish the global two-class unconstrained minimax formula, full signed versus same-sign frontier, constructive sampler, and strict-cost criterion; then complete the full four-unit mirrored three-class phase diagram.
